{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABiIfDPg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhLgMso", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 176, "title": "Suspend gameplay in hidden tabs and resume automatically unless manually paused", "body": "## Motivation

The maintainer has reconsidered the visibility policy introduced in #160 / PR #161. A hidden tab should **automatically suspend gameplay and audio**, but returning to that tab should **automatically resume only gameplay that was intended to be running**. The original problematic behavior was leaving the user in a persistent Pause state after a tab switch; do not bring that behavior back.

Also, use the familiar SNES terminology **Reset**, rather than Restart, for the player action that resets the machine and preserves battery-backed SRAM.

Baseline inspected: `main` at `7a039b0c0aec8aceea5058a45bfc024f451885dd` (PR #175). In [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js), the visibilitychange handler currently only clears input when hidden, and `animate()` runs whenever `playing` is true. The separate `stopPlayback()`, `pause()`, `start()`, cartridge-loading and save-restoration paths already exist. [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) currently renders the button as **Reset**, and the README already uses that term. The Reset label therefore appears to be satisfied already in current source; verify the published UI and any other user-visible labels, correct an actual inconsistency if found, and do not rename internal APIs or add a needless change just to fulfill this item.

## Intended behavior

| Before hiding | While hidden | On becoming visible |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Playing | Automatically suspended; no emulated frames or queued game audio | Automatically continues, without an extra Play click |
| Manually paused | Remains paused | Remains paused |
| No inserted cartridge | Idle | Idle |
| Error or blocked save restoration | Remains stopped/blocked as required | Does not automatically override the error or storage protection |

- Use the Page Visibility API (`document.hidden` / `visibilitychange`) for tab visibility. Losing keyboard focus by itself (e.g. using another control, browser chrome, file picker or another visible window) is not a reason to suspend playback.
- Distinguish deliberate playback intent from a temporary visibility suspension. A hide/show transition must not turn an explicit Pause into Play, and repeated visibility events must not overwrite the resume decision. No new setting, preference, or permanent UI element is needed.
- While hidden, stop emulated-frame advancement even if a browser still delivers animation callbacks. Clear held keyboard/touch inputs and flush queued audio promptly. Resume from the exact emulated state, resetting the wall-clock pacing/debt so time spent hidden cannot cause fast-forward or an audio backlog.
- On visibility return, resume automatically only if still intended to play and safe to do so. Never reload/reset the cartridge or bypass current error/loading/restore guards. Do not steal focus from other controls or re-enter fullscreen. Handle browser audio policy gracefully; try to resume existing audio when appropriate, keep mute/volume unchanged, and do not block gameplay waiting for a gesture or a pending AudioContext promise. Existing sound recovery feedback remains applicable.
- A user-initiated load (bundled demo, local file, saved IndexedDB cartridge) that completes while hidden must remain suspended until visible, then start automatically if successful. Likewise, a valid explicit Reset or Play operation while hidden may establish playback intent, but must not advance emulation until visible. A failed/cancelled load, explicit manual pause, fatal core error or failed restore must not leave stale auto-resume intent that overrides the correct existing lifecycle outcome.
- Preserve the existing battery-backed SRAM identity and save/restore protection. Persist SRAM at the automatic suspension boundary where appropriate and retain pagehide saving; do not discard pending recoverable data or clear persistence errors. Respect existing explicit pause/reset/cartridge save behavior. No change to the IndexedDB ROM library, save format, or game binaries.
- **Reset** keeps the existing semantics: reset volatile machine state while retaining SRAM, then start playing (or remain temporarily suspended if hidden). Verify the actual visible label/accessibility name is Reset, not Restart. Current source is already labeled Reset; if no mismatch is found, record that no label patch was necessary.

## Clean implementation

Prefer one coherent playback model (user/lifecycle intent and effective running state) with simple state transitions. Reuse existing input, audio and SRAM lifecycle helpers. Avoid scattered visibility booleans, duplicated manual/automatic pause implementations, legacy mode flags, unnecessary compatibility shims, timers that simulate background frames, and speculative abstractions. Replace obsolete #160-specific comments, tests and README wording. The visibility behavior above intentionally supersedes #160; preserve the original goal of predictable operation without retaining the old behavior as an option.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] A real Wasm game running in a visible tab stops advancing frames and retains its framebuffer during a simulated hidden period **even when rAF callbacks continue**. Audio is flushed and held keyboard/touch inputs are released. Returning visible resumes frames and fresh audio without any Play click, with normal pacing and no accumulated catch-up.
- [ ] Cover a browser withholding rAF callbacks during a long hidden interval, multiple hide/show cycles, duplicate visibility events and rapid transitions. Verify the manual Pause state and its retained Pixel/CRT image survive all transitions, with no automatic resume. Ordinary blur/focus changes do not change playback intent.
- [ ] Cover in-flight bundled/local/IndexedDB cartridge loading and SRAM restore while hidden, successful retry restore, explicit Reset/Play/Pause interactions, cancelled/failed cartridge selection, fatal errors, empty state, and persistence failures. The new visibility policy must not undo a manual or error-driven stop, silently overwrite SRAM, or break the ROM library's cancellation and deduplication behavior.
- [ ] Test input after resuming, volume/mute, audio blocked/unavailable/pending recovery, Pixel/CRT and fullscreen transitions on desktop/touch. Verify no stale keys, frame bursts, audio backlog, unintended focus or fullscreen changes. Keep all twelve SNES touch controls and existing control placement.
- [ ] Update the existing affected assertions in `web/tests/display.spec.js`, `demo-launch.spec.js`, `touch.spec.js`, `reset.spec.js` and other relevant tests. Reuse the visibility helper in `web/tests/playback.js` where appropriate. Test actual guest progression and audio rather than only button text; do not weaken existing regression checks. Include saved ROM library coverage.
- [ ] Verify Reset remains the visible button label in current source, accessible UI and deployed player. Preserve reset-to-playing and SRAM retention; if source is already correct, do not manufacture a rename.
- [ ] Update README briefly: hidden tabs suspend gameplay, visible tabs resume only if previously intended to play; explicit Pause remains paused. No additional persistent controls or explanatory UI required.
- [ ] Run the production Wasm/site build, applicable full browser/Pages suite and required repository checks. Report actual results, skipped optional device checks and limitations; do not hide known unrelated CI failures (#157/#159) or weaken mandatory assertions.

## Post-merge verification

After merging, confirm the new main GitHub Pages workflow and live published emulator. Start a game, switch tabs, return and verify the same game resumes automatically. Repeat from manual Pause and confirm it stays paused. Check Reset label and behavior. Record the actual deployment revision, workflow and browser evidence; if a confirmed regression remains, track it in a linked task. Post-merge verification is not a pre-merge gate.

Related: #160 / PR #161 (superseded visibility behavior), #128 (Reset), #164 (fullscreen), #170 (persistent ROM library), #174 (performance work; keep that independent).
